It interrupts a job, creates target/produce, work/main.rs and a resume-mark file, then calls drain::drain with a zero budget. It asserts target/ is gone, the work file and the mark are unchanged, the job is still Dispatched, and a registered running job keeps its target/.

summary: The change passes: all seven criteria are met and nothing blocks it. It redoes job 20261101-102128-b1st. At the start of `athena drain` and before each run, the drain now removes `target/` of any job that is dispatched with no closing record, has no registry entry and has a free job lock. Work trees, candidates, resume marks and records stay. A new disk gate in run/mod.rs runs after the baseline checks and before the producer, and holds the job through hold_for_disk as the environment stop `environment: low disk`, with no candidate and no resume mark. I ran the three new tests (drain entry point, reclaim versus running jobs, pre-producer hold) and all passed. fmt, clippy and the full test suite pass in Athena's recorded CI results for this commit. The CHANGELOG and the drain.rs and disk.rs module docs describe the behavior, and the defaults and config files are untouched. Findings: one minor, because two test-only files (run/tests.rs, test_support.rs) are changed but not on the deliverables list, and one nit, for some doc lines that run past the wrap width. Both results come from this snapshot only.
